title: Soft reservations, preemptive burst policy, and tenant isolation tiers for Dedicated capacity
creator: Jamie Alvarez
description: Introduce a soft reservation model and a preemptive burst policy for Dedicated capacity that lets tenants reserve a guaranteed baseline while allowing controlled short-term bursting with graceful preemption. Provide configurable tenant isolation tiers (shared, soft-isolated, hard-isolated) and the console/API UX to manage them. Goals: increase utilization, reduce cold capacity waste, and offer predictable SLAs for enterprise customers.
background: Customers have requested more flexible ways to reserve capacity without paying for permanently idle GPUs. Current reserved pools are rigid: fixed commit sizes with hard guarantees and limited burst semantics. This forces either overcommitment (wasting spend) or frequent manual adjustments. Past incidents (INC-2025-11) showed capacity fragmentation during peak events and poor tenant experience when we preempted without graceful fallback. Engineering has prototype kernels for faster preemption and KV cache snapshotting (ENG-4780).
goals: 1) Offer 'soft reservations' where customers commit to a baseline and get preferential routing and quick warmup within a bounded burst window. 2) Implement a preemptive burst policy: configurable burst duration, max tokens/sec uplift, and graceful preemption hooks for requests. 3) Define and surface three tenant isolation tiers with clear trade-offs and SLAs. 4) Expose controls in Console and API; ensure billing reflects soft reservation usage semantics.
non_goals: 1) Replacing Dedicated's hard committed pools today (that remains available). 2) Implementing custom per-request QoS beyond the scope of burst windows. 3) Modifying model-level kernel selection optimizations (engineering will reuse existing runtime kernels).
requirements: R1: Soft reservation resource model: customer declares baseline vGPU units and a burst allowance (e.g., 20% of baseline) with burst window (e.g., 5m).

R2: Preemptive burst controller in runtime: allow runtime to preempt burst traffic when higher-priority real-time traffic needs capacity; provide graceful preemption signals (HTTP 429 with Retry-After and optional KV cache continuation token).
R3: Isolation tiers: shared (best-effort), soft-isolated (soft reservations + burst), hard-isolated (current reserved pool semantics).
R4: Billing semantics: baseline billed as reserved capacity monthly; burst billed as metered on usage per-minute at a premium rate. Clear invoicing line items and console cost preview.
R5: Console UX: new dedicated capacity page to configure baseline, burst parameters, isolation tier, and view burst usage timeline and expected costs.
R6: API: support new fields on reservation objects (baseline_units, burst_percent, burst_window_seconds, isolation_tier).
R7: SLAs and SLOs: baseline must meet 99.9% allocation and latency SLOs during steady-state; burst best-effort but governed by preemptive rules. Metrics exported to existing tracing/observability.
R8: Migration: existing reserved pools must be convertible to hard-isolated reservations; customers can opt-in to soft reservations with a migration checklist.
ux_requirements: UX1: A configuration wizard with recommended defaults based on recent 30d usage (Console suggests baseline and burst settings).
UX2: Visual timeline showing burst events, preemptions, and cost delta compared to a fixed reservation.
UX3: In-console simulator: estimate probability of preemption given historic cluster load and selected burst settings.
UX4: Clear tooltips that explain trade-offs between isolation tiers and a link to SLA text.
api_changes: POST /dedicated/reservations -> accept baseline_units, burst_percent, burst_window_seconds, isolation_tier; returns reservation_id and estimated cost_preview_url.
PATCH /dedicated/reservations/{id} -> allow changing burst settings; changes take effect at next billing window unless force_apply=true.
Events: emit reservation.preemption.triggered to customer event stream with reason and safe_resume_token where applicable.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Customers can create a soft reservation via API/Console and see a cost preview before committing.
AC2: Runtime honors baseline allocation for soft reservations 99.9% of the time in a synthetic steady-state test run at 80% cluster utilization.

AC3: Burst events can be initiated and terminated; when preemption occurs, in-flight requests receive preemption signals and can be retried with a provided token. Documented sample client retry pattern included.
AC4: Console shows burst usage and preemption events within 1 minute of occurrence; billing records burst usage at minute granularity and appears on a test invoice sample in the billing sandbox.
AC5: Migration path: convert an existing reserved pool to hard-isolated reservation without downtime in staging and documented steps for customers.
success_metrics: SM1: 20% reduction in unused reserved capacity hours across customers who adopt soft reservations within 90 days.
SM2: <2% customer-reported disruptions attributable to preemption during first 3 months after launch.
SM3: >30% of eligible Dedicated customers opt-in to soft reservations within 6 months if pricing differential is favorable.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Alpha): internal tenants + 3 existing enterprise customers. Validate runtime preemption and billing records in sandbox (4 weeks). Phase 2 (Beta): invite list of customers and open Console controls; run a 4-week pilot and gather telemetry and UX feedback. Phase 3 (GA): expose to self-serve with clear docs, migration guides, and SRE playbooks. Rollback: allow customers to switch to hard-isolated reservation immediately; runtime supports an emergency 'no-burst' kill-switch.
migration_and_compatibility: Existing committed pools remain unchanged. Provide a one-click conversion for admins to convert existing pools to hard-isolated reservations. Soft reservations require no infra changes for customers but will alter billing lines; provide billing sandbox and email notification before GA. Backwards compatible API: old reservation endpoints still supported and map to hard-isolated tier by default.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misconfigure burst settings and experience unexpected preemptions. Mitigation: conservative safe defaults, console simulator, and opt-in gating for GA.
Risk: Billing disputes due to metered burst charges. Mitigation: billing sandbox, test invoice, and 30-day grace credits for early adopters; clear invoice line-items and audit logs.

Risk: Runtime preemption causing client-level failure modes (loss of KV cache state). Mitigation: provide safe_resume_token and sample client libraries that know how to resume from token; engineering to instrument cache snapshot/restore hooks.
open_questions: Q1: What is the recommended default burst_percent? (Engineering suggests 15-25% based on cluster variability; product to choose).
Q2: How long should preemption backoff be in client libraries? (UX and runtime to agree on a pattern; default Retry-After recommended).
Q3: Legal: are there regulatory billing disclosure requirements for burst metering? (Finance/legal to confirm).
